newsitem.title: USA: Aviation Sales says it mulling acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Aviation Sales says it mulling acquisitions.

text.p: Aviation Sales Co, an aircraft spare parts redistributor, said it is considering making several acquisitions as the industry consolidates.
"There are four or five acquisition possibilities, some of which are very, very interesting," said Aviation Sales Chairmain Dale Baker, speaking at a conference here.

At the Dillon Read Airlines, Aviation Services & Logistics Conference, Baker said the aircraft parts distribution industry will see rapid consolidation over the next three to four years, with only a handful of major companies remaining.
Industry growth has been fueled, in part, by the "ValuJet situation," Baker said.
The crash of a ValuJet Inc aircraft last year in the Florida Everglades renewed a concern over safety.

"The ValuJet situation sparked a flight of quality. Airlines became more concerned about documentation and traceability of aircraft parts. Airlines began shifting away from Mom and Pop businesses and put their trust in the few main companies out there," Baker said.
Separately, Aviation Sales said it will continue to explore long-term partnerships with airlines and will focus on cost-cutting.
